title: Rethymno or Chania: Which Should You Base Yourself In?
seoTitle: Rethymno or Chania? A Side-by-Side Comparison
seoDescription: Old towns, beaches, crowds, prices, airport distance and day-trip range compared - and a straight answer on which Cretan city to base your holiday in.
summary: Choose Chania for a short trip built around the most beautiful harbour in Crete and the beaches and gorges of the far west; choose Rethymno for a longer stay, a sandy beach that starts where the old town ends, lower prices, quieter evenings, and a central position that puts both halves of the island within a day's drive. Chania's old town is larger and more spectacular but also far busier and more expensive, and its own town beach is small, so beach days mean driving 40 to 75 kilometres. Rethymno's old town is smaller and more lived-in, with a stronger Ottoman layer, and its beach runs about 12 kilometres east from the harbour. If you have three days, go to Chania. If you have a week and a car, base in Rethymno and drive to Chania for a day.
body:
Both are Venetian port cities on Crete's north coast, sixty kilometres apart, and both are genuinely worth your time. They are not interchangeable, and the difference that matters is not really beauty - it is position.

## Side by side

| | Rethymno | Chania |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Size** | Roughly 30,000 people; Crete's third city | Roughly 55,000 in the town; Crete's second city |
| **Old town** | Compact, walkable in about 15 minutes; Venetian streets with a strong Ottoman layer - minarets, wooden bay windows | Larger and more spectacular, wrapped around the Venetian harbour; the arsenali, the covered market, the Splantzia quarter |
| **Landmark** | The Fortezza, built 1573-1580, on the hill above the town | The Egyptian lighthouse at the end of the harbour mole |
| **Town beach** | Sand, starting at the old harbour and running east about 12 km | Nea Chora - small, and the only one in walking distance |
| **Best beaches** | South coast coves near Plakias, ~40 km | Balos, Falasarna and Elafonisi, 55-75 km west |
| **Crowds** | Busy in August, manageable the rest of the year | One of the most visited places in Greece; the harbour is crowded from June to September |
| **Prices** | Noticeably lower for old-town accommodation and dining | Higher, particularly around the harbour |
| **Nearest airport** | CHQ ~70 km (~1 h); HER ~85 km (~1 h 15) | CHQ ~14 km (~20 min) |
| **Day-trip range** | Central - reaches west Crete and east Crete from the same bed | Excellent for west Crete; the east is a long day out and back |
| **Suits** | A week or more, a car, a mix of beach and touring, lower budget, off-season | Three to five days, the postcard version, west Crete, higher budget |

## The old towns

**Chania's** is the better one to look at. The Venetian harbour is a horseshoe of coloured facades with the Egyptian lighthouse closing the far end, and behind it the streets run back through the arsenali - the old Venetian shipyards - into the Splantzia quarter and the covered market. It is bigger than Rethymno's and there is more of it to get lost in. It is also, in high season, extremely full, and the front row of harbour restaurants is the least good food in the city.

**Rethymno's** is smaller and quieter, and it is still in ordinary use. The Ottoman layer is stronger here: the Neratze minaret, wooden upper storeys overhanging the lanes, and the Rimondi Fountain of 1626 running in a small square in the middle. Above it stands the Fortezza, a Venetian fortress from 1573-1580, largely a shell but with the best view in the city from its walls. Rethymno's old town is a fifteen-minute walk across, which is small enough to know properly in two days.

One useful, unglamorous difference: because the University of Crete's humanities campus is in Rethymno, its old town has bookshops, student cafes and year-round restaurants. It does not shut down in November.

## Beaches

This is the clearest practical difference between the two.

**Rethymno's beach starts where the old town ends.** Sand, shallow entry, running east for about 12 kilometres, part organised and part empty. You can swim in the afternoon and walk to dinner. When the north wind blows it gets choppy, and the answer is a 40-kilometre drive over the mountains to the south coast near Plakias, where the coves are small, quiet and sheltered.

**Chania's town beach is Nea Chora**, and it is small. The famous beaches of western Crete - Balos, Falasarna, Elafonisi - are 55 to 75 kilometres away and each is a committed day trip, with Balos additionally requiring either a rough track or a boat from Kissamos. They are spectacular, and they are not a spontaneous afternoon.

## Crowds and prices

Chania's harbour is among the most photographed places in Greece, and the crowd reflects that from June to September. Rethymno is busy in August and comfortable the rest of the year.

On cost, Chania is the more expensive city - old-town accommodation and harbour-front dining both price higher than the Rethymno equivalents. Neither is expensive by western European standards, but over a week the difference is real, and it buys more nights or a better hotel in Rethymno.

## Airports and transfers

Chania wins outright here. Chania airport (CHQ) sits on the Akrotiri peninsula about 14 kilometres from the town - a twenty-minute transfer.

Rethymno has no airport. It is about 70 kilometres and an hour from CHQ, or about 85 kilometres and an hour and a quarter from Heraklion (HER). The upside of being between the two is that you can fly into one and out of the other without backtracking, which widens your flight options considerably.

## Day-trip range - the real argument

Rethymno sits roughly in the middle of the island's north coast, 60 kilometres from Chania and 78 from Heraklion. That is the whole case for it.

| Destination | From Rethymno | From Chania |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Samaria Gorge trailhead (Omalos) | ~100 km | ~40 km |
| Imbros Gorge | ~65 km | ~55 km |
| Elafonisi | ~130 km | ~75 km |
| Balos | ~115 km + track or boat | ~55 km + track or boat |
| Preveli and the south coast | ~40 km | ~100 km |
| Arkadi Monastery | ~23 km | ~85 km |
| Knossos and the Heraklion museum | ~80 km | ~140 km |
| Spinalonga and Elounda | ~130 km | ~190 km |
| The other city | 60 km | 60 km |

From Chania, everything in the western third of Crete is close and everything east of Heraklion is impractical. From Rethymno, the west costs you an extra half hour and the east becomes possible: Knossos is a seven-hour day, Spinalonga a nine-hour one. If your list has both Samaria and Knossos on it, Rethymno is the only base that does not involve moving hotels.

## Who each one suits

**Go to Chania if:** you have three to five days; you want the single most beautiful town in Crete and are willing to share it; your priorities are the western beaches, Samaria and Sfakia; you are flying in and out of CHQ and do not want a long transfer; you would rather have a shorter, more concentrated trip.

**Go to Rethymno if:** you have a week or more; you want to see both halves of the island from one base; you want to swim and then walk to dinner; you are travelling on a tighter budget; you are coming outside July and August; you want somewhere that still functions as a town rather than as a destination.

## Or do both

They are an hour apart, which makes the argument slightly artificial. Two sensible plans:

- **One base, one day trip.** Stay in Rethymno, drive to Chania for a day - old town, harbour, market, dinner, back. You get the postcard without paying to sleep in it.
- **Two bases over ten days.** Four nights in Chania for the west, then six in Rethymno for the centre and east. Move once, not repeatedly - Crete is four hours end to end and hotel-hopping eats the holiday.

faqs.q: Should I stay in Rethymno or Chania?
faqs.a: Chania for a short trip focused on western Crete and the best old-town atmosphere on the island. Rethymno for a week or more, because it sits midway along the north coast and both Samaria in the west and Knossos in the east are day trips from the same hotel. Rethymno also has a long sandy beach at the edge of its old town, which Chania does not.

faqs.q: Which is more beautiful, Rethymno or Chania?
faqs.a: Chania. Its Venetian harbour with the Egyptian lighthouse is the most striking urban scene in Crete, and the old town behind it is larger and richer. Rethymno's old town is smaller and less dramatic, but more lived-in, quieter and considerably cheaper to stay in.
Yes, noticeably - for old-town accommodation and for dining, particularly compared with Chania's harbour front. Over a week the difference is enough to buy extra nights or a better room.

faqs.q: Can I visit Chania as a day trip from Rethymno?
faqs.a: Easily. The two are 60 km apart on the national road, about an hour's drive, and there are frequent intercity buses. A day trip covering the old town, the harbour, the covered market and dinner works well, and it means you get Chania without paying Chania room rates.

Rethymno for convenience - about 12 km of sand starting at the old harbour, plus the sheltered south-coast coves near Plakias 40 km away. Chania for spectacle - Balos, Falasarna and Elafonisi are among the best beaches in Greece, but they are 55 to 75 km west and each one is a full day.

faqs.q: Which city is closer to Samaria Gorge?
faqs.a: Chania. The trailhead at Omalos is about 40 km from Chania and about 100 km from Rethymno. Guided days from Rethymno handle that by starting at 06:30, so it is doable from either - it just costs you an earlier alarm from Rethymno.

faqs.q: Which is better for a first visit to Crete?
faqs.a: If the trip is under five days, Chania - it concentrates the most photogenic parts of the island into the smallest radius. If it is a week or more and you want variety rather than a single postcard, Rethymno, because it puts both halves of Crete within reach without changing hotels.
